thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER: continuous-batching service reported sudden token latency spike + KV cache growth at high concurrency. alert: cb_perf_cliff_high_concurrency. routing to eng-oncall, tag:sev-2

Alice M: saw it too, dashboards - 99th token latency jumped from 150ms -> 1.2s for a subset of requests

Dmitri K: looking at metrics, KV cache entries exploding on shard-7/8, eviction rate can't keep up. batch queue length spiked and microbatch size collapsed -> extra serialization overhead

Eva S: @Dmitri any recent rollout to continuous-batch config?

Dmitri K: yes, yesterday we pushed `cb.default.microbatch_target = 32` -> `64` for perf improvements. Seems under high fanout this increases memory pressure on KV cache because more live KV states retained.

Bob H: customer impact: 3 enterprise customers showing increased 5xx and timeouts. Error budget burn ~12% for two hours. Need to contain before escalation to SEV1.

Alice M: initial mitigation proposal: 1) revert microbatch_target to 32 on affected region, 2) temporarily clamp max_concurrency_per_shard to reduce hot spots, 3) disable prefix KV caching for shards 7/8 to allow faster evictions.

SRE Pager: agreed. I'm taking runbook. Calling step 1 now: revert config rollout for `cb-microbatch-variant` in us-west-2 canary pool.

deploy-bot: Revert apply started for config `cb-microbatch-variant` -> rolling to 6 hosts in canary (shard mapping: 7,8,12)

Eva S: while revert runs, we should apply runtime throttle: `max_inflight_per_route=100` down from 400 for top routes to throttle traffic spikes. That should reduce queue pile-up.

Dmitri K: adding a small jitter reduction too: `batch_jitter_ms = 8` -> `3`. Less jitter reduces microbatch formation variability under extreme concurrency.

Alice M: FYI, KV cache TTL for conversational prefix cache is 20m on these shards; propose dropping to 5m as temporary. That will reduce working set.

SRE Pager: doing these as a coordinated mitigation. I'm going to create a short maintenance window note and notify CS.

Bob H: Customer comms: Two impacted customers (cust-id: ACME-42, FinApps-Prod). Error rates peaked ~18% for ACME-42; FinApps partial degradation for long-context calls only. CS is preparing targeted message.

Dmitri K: observability note: enabling additional KV telemetry on shard 7 to capture per-key lifetimes and eviction churn. Might add noise; rolling carefully.

deploy-bot: Revert finished on 6 canary hosts: 6/6 succeeded; staging metrics show 30% drop in 99th token latency for canary. Proceeding to gradual rollout to remaining hosts (12 hosts)

Alice M: hold rollout at 50% for 10m to verify KV growth stabilizes. If stable, continue. If it regresses, we abort and force-disable continuous batching on that node set.

SRE Pager: CS notified via #customer-status and created incident update for affected customers with ETA 30m for next update.

Eva S: small config snippet we're applying via patch: ```
- cb.default.microbatch_target: 64
+ cb.default.microbatch_target: 32
  cb.runtime.batch_jitter_ms: 3
  cb.runtime.max_inflight_per_route: 100
  kv.cache.prefix_ttl_sec: 300
```

Bob H: tracking impact on SLOs: maintainers, please log any 5xx traces with `trace.tag:cb_kv_surge` so we can tie regressions back to the batch config change.

Dmitri K: quick root-cause hypothesis: increasing microbatch target lengthened KV lifetime because multi-step generation with larger microbatches pinned KV cache references longer; under high concurrency this amplifies working set and eviction thrash -> perf cliff. Will follow up with memory profile.

Alice M: if revert + throttles don't bring error rate under 2% in 20m, next step is to enable fallback routing to lower-capacity model variant for high-concurrency routes to avoid customer-visible timeouts.

SRE Pager: monitoring: adding alert rule to watch `kv.cache.size` growth and `batch.queue.length` with immediate paging if either crosses emergency threshold. Also documenting handoff steps for next on-call.

Bob H: CS update: emailed ACME-42 with mitigation steps and ETA. FinApps on a call; they want postmortem once stable. Keep them in the loop.

deploy-bot: Rollout 50% -> success after 8m, canary metrics look stable (kv growth down 42%, 99p latency back within baseline). Continuing remaining 50% in 5m.

Alice M: good. @Dmitri after this incident we need a mitigation in runtime: auto-detect KV growth by per-shard working set delta and dynamically reduce `microbatch_target` or disable prefix caching preemptively. Add to tech backlog with priority P0 for infra.

Dmitri K: agreed; will add a short RFC and prototype a circuit-breaker that reduces microbatch_target when eviction rate > 200/s for > 30s.

SRE Pager: logging final status: mitigation applied, customers showing recovery, continuing to monitor for 60m. Passing to follow-up owners: @Dmitri (root cause), @Alice (postmortem & customer comms), @Eva (runtime mitigations). If anything regresses ping me.

Bob H: closing loop: please add timeline notes and attach relevant dashboards to the incident ticket.

Alice M: will draft postmortem and include config diffs and repro steps. Thanks team :tada:
